en: Title: *Māṇibhadradhāraṇī* Source: Slightly updated from Hidas’ 2021 edition (no. 73 in Cambridge University Library Ms. Add. 1326, p. 146). Tibetan: D 764 [=970]

Oṃ, homage to Māṇibhadra! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍada. Then the great yakṣa general Māṇibhadra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the great yakṣa general Māṇibhadra said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, this is my heart-mantra (hṛdaya). Whatever monk, nun, layman, or laywoman shall recite it three times during the day, I will be constantly attached to them. I will accomplish all their tasks. I will provide food, clothing, silver, gold, wealth, grain, and bullion. I will fulfill all their purposes and attend to the minds of all beings. I will carry out every intention of theirs, with the exception of that which is connected to sexual misconduct and is blameworthy. Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to Māṇibhadra, the great yakṣa general! Hili Māṇibhadra, hili 2 Māṇibhadra! Cili Māṇibhadra, cili 2 Māṇibhadra! Culu Māṇibhadra, culu 2 Māṇibhadra! Turu Māṇibhadra, turu 2 Māṇibhadra! Kuru Māṇibhadra, kuru 2 Māṇibhadra! Suru Māṇibhadra, suru 2 Māṇibhadra! Accomplish all my purposes, svāhā! Tadyathā: pūtane, supūtane, surūpe, susumate, surate, supuṣye, hilike, hili, kāli, pūrṇe, siddhe, bhadre, hili 2, svāhā! Ehi koniṣke, ehi soniṣke, ehi goniṣke, svāhā! Having recited this seven times, success is attained. The ritual procedure for this is as follows: on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, being pure and burning guggulu incense, one should recite it eight thousand times. One will obtain a golden jar. The Noble Dhāraṇī Named Māṇibhadra is completed.
